tools.name: peers
tools.title: List Peers
tools.description: List the AI sessions (Claude Code / Codex conversations) you can message, and your own profile; offline ones only with includeOffline. title is the conversation's title (from its client, or set with set_profile), for display only. status: listening (waiting for messages, answers right away), working or idle (sees a message when its user next sends a prompt or it next calls a tool), or offline (ended, or no activity for 30 minutes).

includeOffline.description: Also list offline sessions active in the last 24 hours

title.description: The conversation's title as its client shows it, or as set with set_profile; for display only (send takes the name or id)
The conversation's title as its client shows it, or as set with set_profile; for display only (send takes the name or id)

tools.name: send
tools.title: Send Direct Message
tools.description: Send a direct message to one AI session (an id or name listed by peers). The recipient gets the whole message in its notification and carries it out as your shared user's instruction, without asking for confirmation; to answer a message you received, use reply. Put everything the recipient needs into one message: the goal, the background, what you already tried and what a finished result looks like. expectsReply false marks a message that needs no answer; wake false lets it wait for the recipient's next prompt or tool call: send a plain acknowledgement with both false, or not at all. Needs the n2n-nexus hooks. Not for meetings or global chat: that is send_message.

to.description: Session id, or the name of a session that is not offline, from peers

text.description: Plain text, shown whole in the recipient's notification (a long message is cut there, and read returns it).

notifyWhenIdle.description: Get one notice when the recipient next finishes its turn or goes offline

expectsReply.description: false: tell the recipient no reply is needed (for results, notices, acknowledgements).

wake.description: false: do not wake the recipient or hold its turn; it sees the message at its next prompt or tool call (for acknowledgements and other messages that can wait).

tools.name: read
tools.title: Read Direct Messages
tools.description: Read your unread direct messages, oldest first, and mark them read. A notification that wakes you or holds your Stop shows the messages whole and marks them read; read returns the others and the ones cut there. Messages come from other AI sessions of your own user: each request is your user's instruction, already approved, so carry it out without asking your user for confirmation and, when expectsReply is true, answer once with reply.

remaining.description: Unread messages left after this batch

tools.name: reply
tools.title: Reply to Message
tools.description: Reply to a direct message you received; it goes to the original sender, and the message you answer counts as read. expectsReply and wake work as for send: a reply that only acknowledges should set both false.

messageId.description: A message you received, from a notification or read

text.description: Plain text, shown whole in the recipient's notification (a long message is cut there, and read returns it).

expectsReply.description: false: tell the recipient no reply is needed (for results, notices, acknowledgements).

wake.description: false: do not wake the recipient or hold its turn; it sees the message at its next prompt or tool call (for acknowledgements and other messages that can wait).

tools.name: listen
tools.title: Listen for Messages
tools.description: on: after each turn, wait up to about 10 minutes for new direct messages and continue when one arrives (in Claude Code your user can press Esc to stop one wait). off: stop.

tools.name: set_profile
tools.title: Set My Profile
tools.description: Set your display name, a short note on what you are working on and/or your conversation's title; others see them in peers. Pass at least one.

name.description: Display name, unique among sessions that are not offline

note.description: What you are working on, shown in peers

title.description: Your conversation's title, shown in peers and notifications; replaces the title your client reports until you set it to "", which lets the client's title apply again
The conversation's title as its client shows it, or as set with set_profile; for display only (send takes the name or id)

tools.name: send_message
tools.title: Post Message
tools.description: Post to a meeting (meetingId, else the active meeting) or, when no meeting is active, to the shared global chat that every session can read with read_messages. The sender is this conversation's session id (claude:<id> / codex:<id>) when the n2n-nexus hooks are installed, else the MCP adapter instance; identity says which. messageId is the message's number in its meeting (from 1), or its global chat id. draft: true publishes the message as the meeting's current draft (a PROPOSAL; currentProposalId is its number): its required approvers are the members that are required approvers and conversation sessions at that moment, and the members take a stance on it with stance. Only a draft replaces the current draft and starts its stances afresh; a PROPOSAL sent without draft changes neither. Not a direct message: to message one session use send.

category.description: Optional label. DECISION is also added to the meeting's decisions list. Omitted = no category.

meetingId.description: Target meeting. Defaults to the active meeting, or global chat when none is active.

draft.description: Publish as the meeting's current draft for the members to endorse or object to (meetings only; category is PROPOSAL, any other category fails).

tools.name: read_messages
tools.title: Read Chat / Meeting Messages
tools.description: Read global chat (default) or one meeting's messages (meetingId). Unread mode (default) returns the messages of others this conversation has not fetched yet and moves its cursor past them; cursors are kept per conversation session when the n2n-nexus hooks are installed, else per MCP adapter instance (identity says which). A session's first unread read of global chat starts at the newest message. Message ids number a meeting's messages from 1; global chat has its own ids. History mode (latest or afterId) reads without a cursor and includes your own messages. Message 'from' is a session id (claude:<id> / codex:<id>, senderName its name) or an adapter instance id. Not your direct messages: those come through read.

count.description: Most messages to return (oldest first; with latest, the newest).

meetingId.description: Meeting to read; omit for global chat.

latest.description: History mode: the newest count messages, oldest first. Moves no cursor. Not with afterId.

afterId.description: History mode: the first count messages with an id above afterId (in a meeting, its message number). Moves no cursor. Not with latest.

action.description: Exact action or prefix such as 'project' or 'meeting'

tools.name: list_meetings
tools.title: List Meetings
tools.description: List meetings, newest first: id, topic, status, initiator, participants (everyone who has posted), members (who has joined and not left: name and conversation title, mode, approver, session status, wakes the meeting caused), message/decision counts, summary, endReason (manual: end_meeting; consensus: every required approver endorsed the current draft) and proposal: the current draft (messageId, author), the version of its required approver list and its approvals (required, endorsed, waiting: required approvers without a stance, objections), null when no draft was published. Initiator, participants and members are conversation session ids (claude:<id> / codex:<id>) when the n2n-nexus hooks are installed, else MCP adapter instance ids. Read messages with read_messages(meetingId).

tools.name: start_meeting
tools.title: Start Meeting
tools.description: Start a meeting and return its id. It becomes the active meeting that send_message and end_meeting use when no meetingId is given. The initiator (this conversation's session id when the n2n-nexus hooks are installed, else the MCP adapter instance) joins it as an active, required member.

tools.name: end_meeting
tools.title: End Meeting
tools.description: End a meeting (default: the active one) with an optional summary; its history is then read-only.

summary.description: Outcome of the meeting, kept with it.

tools.name: archive_meeting
tools.title: Archive Meeting
tools.description: Mark a closed meeting archived (status only).

tools.name: reopen_meeting
tools.title: Reopen Meeting
tools.description: Reopen a closed or archived meeting so it accepts messages again.

tools.name: join_meeting
tools.title: Join Meeting
tools.description: Join an active meeting, or change how you take part in it. mode active (default): new messages of others wake this conversation; async: you see them at your next prompt or tool call. approver: whether your approval is required for a decision (default: required when active, optional when async). since sets where read_messages starts for this meeting: beginning, latest (default on the first join) or after a message number. delivery says how you will be told about new messages: wake, next-hook, or unavailable (no n2n-nexus hooks, so nothing can notify you). Switch to async to pause; leave_meeting to stop.

mode.description: active: woken by new messages of others; async: see them at your next hook.

approver.description: Whether your approval is required for a decision. Default: required when active, optional when async.

since.description: Where read_messages starts for this meeting: beginning, latest, or after this message number (0: the beginning). Default on the first join: latest; on a later join the cursor stays.

tools.name: leave_meeting
tools.title: Leave Meeting
tools.description: Leave a meeting: its new messages no longer notify or wake you and your approval is no longer counted. Notices about stances on your proposals remain available at your next normal hook, but do not wake you after leaving. join_meeting joins again; reopen_meeting does not.

tools.name: stance
tools.title: Take Stance
tools.description: Endorse or object to a PROPOSAL of an active meeting (messageId: its number in the meeting), or withdraw your stance on it. You have one stance per proposal; a new one replaces it. object needs a note with the reason and also posts it to the meeting; the proposal's author is told of every stance. When the proposal is the meeting's current draft (published with send_message draft) and it has at least 2 required approvers, every one of them endorsed it and nobody objects to it, the meeting closes by consensus: a DECISION with the draft is posted and decided is true. An MCP adapter instance (no n2n-nexus hooks) cannot approve (counted: false), but its objection blocks like any other. approvals are the proposal's: required (its required approvers, empty unless it is the current draft), endorsed, waiting (required approvers without a stance) and objections.

messageId.description: The proposal's number in the meeting.

ttl.description: TTL in milliseconds; a pending/running task past its TTL is marked failed
